correctness.rationale: The all-parameter proof reconstructs. A positive ground state on each gap forces \(0<kd_j<\pi\). Solving the gap endpoint problem yields a real symmetric cyclic Dirichlet-to-Neumann matrix with positive off-diagonal weights \(k\csc(kd_j)\); the strictly positive nodal vector therefore belongs to its largest eigenvalue by Perron--Frobenius after a scalar shift, so that eigenvalue equals \(lpha\). Testing the constant vector gives \(lpha\ge(2k/N)\sum_j\tan(kd_j/2)\). Strict convexity of tangent on the positive branch gives \(lpha\ge2k\tan(\pi k/N)\), with strictness off equal gaps. The equal-gap branch has the constant Perron eigenvector and \(F_N(k)=2k\tan(\pi k/N)\) is strictly increasing, proving unique global optimality for every \(N\ge2\) and \(lpha>0\). The finite transfer-matrix code is not needed for the universal quantifier.
risks: The theorem is restricted to equal positive delta strengths, periodic one-dimensional geometry and the ground state.

originality.rationale: Exner 2019 is the exact motivating primary source: it proves equal spacing only for sufficiently weak repulsion and sufficiently strong repulsion and explicitly states the every-positive-coupling result as Conjecture 5.1. Fresh Resultary searches for repulsive point interactions, periodic loops, equal spacing and all coupling did not locate a covering prior theorem. The sibling N=2 antipodal result is strictly weaker and does not imply the all-\(N\) statement. Thus the final theorem remains original to best knowledge, with the normal residual risk of differently indexed later work.
